newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains rise on continued export optimism.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains rise on continued export optimism.

text.p: LIFFE grain futures rose in active trade on Thursday as export optimism continued to fuel upward momentum.
Continued trade talk of sales to China bolstered wheat in particular, traders said.

"It's still feeding off the China rumour," one trader said, referring to talk of a big shipment being loaded, although he noted that there were still no hard and fast numbers on the amount of business done.
"People are taking a more positive view," he said. There was shipper and consumer buying to be seen and dips were being seen as buying opportunities, he said.
The market had seen the high volume bid for at the EU tender as a positive sign, although the actual tender result had given a more mixed message.
Active May wheat last traded 1.25 stg up at 99.20 stg. May volume was 635 lots of a total 939.
Sterling, which managed to inch above 2.75 marks in late European trading, had little impact.
Barley also rose, with May most active. It last traded at 93.75 stg, 0.80 stg higher. Of a total 70 lots of barley, 42 were on May.
